title: Petition to the bishop for leave to build a wooden chapel, 27 January 1803, page 1
kind: Manuscript petition, photographed original

register.parish: n/a

fields.original: Conspiciendo nosmet ipsos tam miseram, et non stabilem Capellam habere, ideo supplices ad Dominum Nostrum Terrestrem Antonium K. Mihályi concurrimus, qui etiam videndo rectam nostram petitionem, nobis locum pro capella in proprio fundo donavit, quemadmodum ejus Manuscriptum hic involutum exhibet. Ideo nunc unice ad Excellentiam Vestram Praesuleam devotissimi veniendo flexis genibus oramus, quatenus gratioso indultu Excellentiae Vestrae, in eodem loco donato, ligneam Capellam nobis exstruere valeremus. In reliquo Altissimis Praesularibus Gratiis nos commendantes perseveramus Excellentiae Vestrae Praesuleae
fields.english: Seeing that we have so poor and unsound a chapel, we went as petitioners to our landlord, Antonius K. Mihályi, who found our request just and gave us a site for a chapel on his own land, as his enclosed note shows. We now come most humbly to Your Episcopal Excellency alone and beg on bended knee that, by Your Excellency's gracious leave, we may build ourselves a wooden chapel on the site so given. Commending ourselves to your episcopal favour, we remain Your Excellency's
fields.note: Abbreviations expanded. The landlord's name is read 'K. Mihályi'; the initial is not expanded.

translation: To the bishop. The people of Pálócz, Tegenye, Viszoka and Mogyorós say their chapel is poor and unsound. Their landlord, Antonius K. No archive stamp, fond or folio number is visible on this page.
The addressee is not named. 'Praesul' is a bishop; the four villages and the request for a wooden chapel fit a petition from Greek Catholics to the bishop of Mukachevo. That is an inference.
